head.decision_question: Should PaymentHub move to a new settlement core with dual-write during transition?
head.decision_owner: CTO (named in intake, redacted for the public fixture)
head.in_scope: Settlement core, dual-write transition mechanism, schema reconciliation
head.out_of_scope: Card scheme certification, the merchant onboarding portal
head.deadline: Contested — see [Q2.5]; two conflicting statements are on record

Q1.1.text: Settlement reconciliation breaks on roughly 0.4% of transactions and is repaired by a nightly manual process.

Q1.2.text: The exception rate has been stable for two years. The review was triggered by the card scheme's 2027 message-format change.

Q1.3.text: Named by the engineering lead. Operations agrees. Finance considers the manual repair acceptable.

Q1.4.text: A matching-rule rewrite in 2025 reduced the exception rate from 0.9% to 0.4%.

Q1.5.text: Manual repair effort is quantified at 180,000 EUR over 12 months.

Q2.1.text: Should PaymentHub move to a new settlement core with dual-write during transition?

Q2.2.text: The CTO is named as decision owner.

Q2.3.text: Settlement core, dual-write transition mechanism, schema reconciliation.

Q2.4.text: Card scheme certification and the merchant onboarding portal.

Q2.5.text: Two statements are on record and they contradict each other. Statement 1 — CTO at architecture review 2026-08-10: "Decision required by end of Q3 2026." Statement 2 — CFO at budget review 2026-08-15: "Budget cycle runs to Q1 2027; no commitment before then." Neither is adopted here.
Q2.5.source: Statement 1: Architecture review minutes 2026-08-10, ref ARC-2026-44. Statement 2: CFO budget memo 2026-08-15, ref FIN-2026-5001.

Q2.6.text: Settlement exceptions below 0.05% and full compatibility with the 2027 scheme message format.

Q2.7.text: Operations (exception volume), Finance (manual repair cost), Compliance (scheme conformance).

Q3.1.text: The settlement store must remain on the licensed enterprise database; the licence runs to 2029.

Q3.2.text: Budget envelope has not been fixed. The CFO memo defers commitment to the FY2027 cycle.

Q3.3.text: 6 years in production. Roughly one release per month, with a freeze over each month-end settlement window.

Q3.4.text: An annual scheme compliance audit each March constrains changes to the settlement path.

Q3.5.text: Architecture board, then risk committee, then CFO sign-off. Historically 10 to 14 weeks.

Q4.1.text: A settlement core (6 years, Java 21), the licensed enterprise database, a message gateway, and a reconciliation batch.

Q4.2.text: An internal architecture wiki, verified against the running system in May 2026.

Q4.3.text: The reconciliation batch's exception-matching rules are understood by two engineers; no component is fully unowned.

Q4.4.text: Transaction, settlement, and merchant reference data. The settlement store is the single source; merchant reference is read from the onboarding system.

Q4.5.text: Message gateway to the card scheme, ledger export to Finance, and a read from merchant onboarding. All three are documented.

Q4.6.text: Automated coverage 81% line, 93% on the settlement path. Last full regression 2026-08-08.

Q5.1.text: Finance ledger (daily file), merchant portal (sync REST), card scheme gateway (sync message).

Q5.2.text: The card scheme gateway is business-critical: 99.95% availability, p99 under 250ms, contractually fixed.

Q5.3.text: Finance maintains a spreadsheet reconciliation of the daily ledger file. It is documented and agreed.

Q5.4.text: The card scheme interface is contractually fixed. The Finance ledger export is covered by an internal SLA. The merchant portal read is informal.

Q5.5.text: Named accept-authority exists for the scheme gateway and the Finance export. For the merchant portal read it is not established.

Q6.1.text: Transaction data is classified Restricted; merchant reference is Confidential. Validated by the Data Protection Officer.

Q6.2.text: Personal data enters through the transaction message (cardholder reference, merchant contact). Legal basis: contract performance and legal obligation.

Q6.3.text: Head of Payments Operations owns transaction and settlement data; Head of Merchant Services owns merchant reference.

Q6.4.text: Transaction records retained 10 years per financial regulation. Erasure path tested for merchant reference data on 2026-05-14; not applicable to transaction records under the retention obligation.

Q6.5.text: Processing stays within the EU. The scheme gateway terminates in the EU region.

Q7.1.text: PSD2 and GDPR apply; scheme rules apply contractually. Reviewed by Compliance on 2026-02-10.

Q7.2.text: Last scheme compliance audit March 2026. One finding on key rotation cadence, closed June 2026.
Q7.2.source: Audit report SCH-AUD-2026-03 and closure record.

Q7.3.text: No AI/ML in the decision subject. AI is used only in the authoring process of this analysis.
Q7.3.source: Scoping statement, architecture review 2026-08-10, ref ARC-2026-44.

Q7.4.text: Not applicable — AI/ML is not in the decision subject.
Q7.4.source: Scoping statement, architecture review 2026-08-10, ref ARC-2026-44.

Q7.5.text: PCI DSS attestation is maintained annually; the settlement core is in scope.

Q8.1.text: Two paths considered: dual-write transition to a new settlement core, and an in-place message-format uplift on the existing core.

Q8.2.text: One irreversible step: the settlement cut-over. Once the new core becomes the book of record, the old settlement store is closed to writes and cannot be restored as authoritative.

Q8.3.text: Two statements are on record and they contradict each other. Statement 1 — Engineering lead: "Dual-write can be operational in 4 weeks." Statement 2 — DBA team: "Minimum 6 months for schema reconciliation under dual-write." Neither is adopted here.
Q8.3.source: Statement 1: Engineering lead, internal meeting 2026-08-05. Statement 2: DBA team written assessment 2026-08-12, ref DBA-2026-18.

Q8.4.text: Before cut-over, rollback is a routing switch under 30 minutes. After cut-over, no rollback path has been described.

Q8.5.text: Evaluated for the pre-cut-over phase and documented. For the post-cut-over phase it has not been evaluated.

Q8.6.text: Historical transaction records under the 10-year obligation stay in the existing store as a read-only archive; the strategy is documented.

Q9.1.text: The Payments Platform team owns PaymentHub; the accountable lead is named in the intake.

Q9.2.text: Changes arrive through the service catalogue and are reviewed by two engineers plus a DBA for anything touching the settlement schema.

Q9.3.text: Settlement schema knowledge is concentrated in the DBA team; exception-matching knowledge sits with two engineers.

Q9.4.text: No restructuring is planned within the decision window.

Q9.5.text: The DBA team lead holds effective veto over settlement schema changes; no such change has proceeded over their objection.

Q10.1.text: SLO: 99.95% monthly availability on the scheme gateway path. Met for the last 12 months at 99.97%.
Q10.1.source: SRE runbook v5 and availability report.

Q10.2.text: RTO 1 hour, RPO 0 for settlement. The last restore test was scheduled for July 2026 and has not been carried out.

Q10.3.text: Structured logs, RED metrics, traces on the settlement path, and reconciliation exception alerting.

Q10.4.text: Documented incident process with 24/7 on-call and a change process with a month-end freeze. Both exercised in the March audit.
Q10.4.source: SRE runbook v5, audit report SCH-AUD-2026-03.

Q10.5.text: Production access is role-based through the central identity provider with quarterly review; last review 2026-07-01.

Q10.6.text: Encrypted at rest and in transit. Keys are held in a hardware security module, separate from the data.
